name: Carrier-based home console
definition: home console on which the owner loads different games from a carrier, card, download or storage.
notes: list covers consoles that load media; dedicated consoles excluded

name: Dedicated home console
definition: home console with built-in games that the owner cannot load (includes plug-and-play minis).
notes: dedicated consoles have games built in; plug-and-play and Flashback lines

name: Carrier-based handheld
definition: handheld in which games are loaded, not built in; the operating system is an attribute, so a handheld gaming PC is a named form of this kind with os = PC.
notes: cartridge and Android/PC handhelds listed

name: Hybrid console
definition: console that works both docked to a TV and as a handheld.
notes: Switch, Sega Nomad, Shield Portable named as hybrid examples

name: Dedicated LCD handheld
definition: handheld with its game built in on an LCD.
notes: each unit one built-in game on segmented LCD plus clock

name: Standalone VR or mixed-reality headset
definition: headset that encloses the eyes and has its own compute and battery.
notes: Standalone class lists Meta Quest, Pico, HTC Vive Focus

name: Tethered VR headset
definition: headset that encloses the eyes and needs a console or PC as its host (host platform is an attribute).
notes: PC-Powered and Console classes list Vive, Rift, PlayStation VR2

name: Upright cabinet
definition: coin-operated video arcade cabinet that stands upright, played standing.
notes: Upright/Standard category

name: Cabaret (mini) cabinet
definition: smaller upright coin-operated video cabinet.
notes: Cabaret/Mini category

name: Cocktail table cabinet
definition: coin-operated video cabinet built as a table, played seated across or beside it.
notes: Cocktail category

name: Sit-down cabinet (candy cabinet)
definition: coin-operated video cabinet with a seat for the player.
notes: Candy/Japanese category, player sits in a chair

name: Cockpit or environmental cabinet
definition: enclosed or motion cabinet built around the player.
notes: Cockpit/Environmental category

name: Counter-top or bar-top cabinet
definition: small cabinet made to stand on a counter or bar.
notes: Counter-Top/Table-Top/Bar-Top category

name: Disk-drive add-on
definition: unit that adds a disk drive to a console.
notes: Famicom Disk System and Sega CD add drives to a console

name: Cartridge converter
definition: unit that lets a console play cartridges of another system or region.
notes: Super Game Boy, Power Base Converter, Super 8 adapters

name: Gamepad
definition: hand-held controller with a directional pad, buttons and sticks or triggers, held in both hands.
notes: gamepads listed from NES to DualSense

name: Detachable split controller
definition: controller made as two detachable halves that can be used apart.
notes: Joy-Con and Joy-Con 2 listed as motion gamepads

name: Levered arcade stick
definition: arcade-style controller with a joystick lever and buttons.
notes: Hori Real Arcade Pro stick with lever switching; arcade joysticks listed

name: Racing wheel
definition: steering-wheel controller for driving games.
notes: G29 and G920 wheels with pedals; Wii Wheel and neGcon listed

name: Pedal set
definition: set of foot pedals sold as a controller.
notes: T-LCM sold as pedals only; no wheel included

name: Light gun
definition: gun-shaped pointing controller.
notes: NES Zapper, Menacer, Super Scope, Konami Justifier

name: Motion controller
definition: controller that senses its own movement in the player's hand.
notes: Wii Remote, PlayStation Move, Power Glove

name: Console camera
definition: camera made to track the player as game input.
notes: Kinect and PlayStation Camera track players as input

name: Rhythm instrument controller
definition: controller shaped like a musical instrument, made to control a game.
notes: guitar, drum, keyboard and turntable controllers

name: Dance or balance mat
definition: floor mat or board that reads the player's steps or weight as game input.
notes: Power Pad floor mat; Wii Balance Board

name: Leverless (all-button) controller
definition: arcade-style controller with all-button directional input and no lever.
notes: Hit Box and Smash Box replace the stick with four direction buttons

name: Game disc
definition: game on an optical disc.
notes: PS5 game discs hold up to 100 GB

name: Game cartridge
definition: game on a cartridge holding memory chips.
notes: ROM cartridge formats: Game Pak, Genesis, Atari 2600 cartridge

name: Game card
definition: game on a small flash-memory card.
notes: Nintendo Game Card is flash-memory card carrying games

name: Magnetic game media
definition: game on a cassette, floppy or disk-system card.
notes: Famicom Disk System uses proprietary floppy Disk Cards for games

name: Game-key card
definition: physical card that holds only a key to a game, not the game.
notes: game-key card holds a key; game must be downloaded

name: Download-code card or voucher
definition: card or box that unlocks one game as a download.
notes: Nintendo download card unlocks one chosen game via eShop code

name: Digital game licence
definition: full game downloaded on a console or PC store, held with no carrier.
notes: Steam and console stores sell full games as downloads

name: Expansion
definition: downloadable content that adds a large part to a base game.
notes: expansions are larger DLC; Sims 4 expansion packs listed

name: Add-on pack
definition: downloadable maps, levels, characters, artbook or wallpaper content for a game.
notes: add-on packs are smaller DLC; PlayStation Store sells add-ons

name: Game mod
definition: modification that adds to or changes one game.
notes: mods alter or add to an existing game; ModDB catalogues them

name: Case or pouch
definition: case or pouch made to hold or protect one game machine.
notes: Switch carry case with screen protector; PowerA protection case

name: Screen protector film
definition: film for the screen of one game machine.
notes: Carry Case & Screen Protector set for Switch; film shown only inside a set

name: Battery pack made for one machine
definition: rechargeable battery pack made for one game machine or controller.
notes: Battery class lists Joy-Con, Wii U GamePad, Xbox 360 packs

name: AC adapter
definition: power adapter made for one game machine.
notes: AC adapters listed per console

name: Charging stand or dock (charging only)
definition: stand or dock that only charges the machine or controller.
notes: DualSense Charging Station charges two controllers without console

name: Proprietary cable or adapter
definition: cable or adapter with a proprietary connector made for one console.
notes: Xbox 360 Play and Charge Cable, VGA HD AV Cable, Xbox SCART Adaptor

name: Proprietary memory card or expansion
definition: memory card, drive or expansion in a format made only for one console.
notes: Xbox 360 Memory Unit, GameCube Memory Card, N64 Controller Pak

name: TV dock
definition: dock that gives video output to a TV as well as charging.
notes: Switch Dock HAC-007 and Switch 2 Dock BEE-005

name: Stand or mount
definition: stand or mount made to hold one game machine.
notes: Switch Stand HAC-062; PS4 Vertical Stand

name: Multitap
definition: unit that adds controller ports to a console.
notes: Super Multitap and Genesis 4-Player Adaptor listed as multiplayer interfaces

name: Cheat device
definition: cartridge or unit that alters a game (Game Genie type).
notes: Pro Action Replay and Mega Key 2 listed as modification tools

name: Replacement part or repair tool
definition: spare part or tool for repairing a game machine or controller.
notes: Jumper Pak Ejector Tool NUS-012 listed as modification tool; spare-part coverage thin

name: Flight stick
definition: joystick controller for flight games.
notes: Saitek X52 and Thrustmaster HOTAS Warthog flight sticks

name: Faceplate, skin or decal
definition: cover plate, skin or decal that changes the outside of one game machine or controller.
notes: dbrand skins and wraps for Switch consoles and controllers

name: Toys-to-Life portal or reader
definition: portal or reader that reads Toys-to-Life figures for a game.
notes: Portal of Power reads Skylanders figures; portal per game generation
